name: Crowdin
tagline: Manage a software localization project with file sync, glossary, and reviews

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Free plan confirmed; current official page did not expose its numeric project, hosted-word, string, or manager caps in accessible content
tiers.notes: Open-source and academic licenses, if approved, include unlimited projects, strings, and members; those are separate eligibility programs.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Personal/small-team localization plan; hosted-word and manager allowance not exposed in accessible official pricing content

tiers.name: Team
tiers.limits: Price is customized by hosted words and managers; unlimited translators/proofreaders; 14-day trial
tiers.notes: Official billing documentation uses $179/month or $1,800/year as the current Team-plan example.

tiers.name: Team+
tiers.limits: Organization plan; official billing documentation gives $5,400/year; exact included hosted words/managers not exposed

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Organization plan with SAML SSO, teams, and IP allowlisting; 30-day Enterprise trial includes Business features
tiers.notes: Annual only; current public amount was not exposed in accessible official content.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Custom organization plan; projects, hosted words, managers, security, and services negotiated

pricing.freeTierCaps: Free plan exists, but its current numeric project/hosted-word/manager caps were not exposed in accessible official pricing content
pricing.billingTerms: Crowdin personal/team plans monthly + annual (annual gives 2 months free); Crowdin Enterprise plans annual only; taxes excluded
pricing.hiddenCosts: Price scales with managers and hosted words, where hosted words = source words × target languages; over-limit access can be suspended after a grace period; paid marketplace apps, AI/MT/pro translation credits, managed services, and CDN usage above 1M requests + 10GB are separate.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Crowdin, manage a software localization project with file sync, glossary, and reviews. The hard boundary is large integration ecosystem, translators, marketplace, workflows, and enterprise governance, plus translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations.
coreLoopDIY: Manage a software localization project's translation keys with file sync, a glossary, and reviews, preserve context, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings.
requirements: optional DeepL or OpenAI API key
whatYouLose: large integration ecosystem, translators, marketplace, workflows, and enterprise governance
moatNotes: translation memory, collaboration, and deployment integrations
ongoingBurden: file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Crowdin because localization teams pay because language context, review discipline, translators, and release integrations are the hard parts. The recurring cost buys file formats, placeholders, plural rules, screenshots, context, permissions, review, glossary, machine translation, sync, and backups, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Tolgee
priorArt.desc: Active open-source localization platform with translation memory and in-context tooling.

alternatives.name: Tolgee
alternatives.desc: In-context translation, screenshots, memory, terminology, review and CI integrations in a much smaller bill.

facts.install: Hosted Tolgee Cloud signup or the official Docker Compose deployment with PostgreSQL
facts.engines: Tolgee's contextual AI translator and machine-translation layer can connect to Google Cloud Translation, Amazon Translate, DeepL, Microsoft Azure Translator, Baidu, and configured LLM/MT providers.
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted projects, keys, translations, users, and translation memory live in PostgreSQL, while screenshots and uploaded files live under the persistent data directory; cloud accounts store the same classes of data on Tolgee infrastructure.
facts.gapVsPaid: Tolgee has fewer marketplace, vendor-management, enterprise permission, repository, design-tool, and workflow integrations than Crowdin at scale.
facts.setupBlocker: None for cloud signup; self-hosting needs Docker, an external PostgreSQL database, persistent file storage, mail/domain/TLS, backups, and provider keys for third-party translation engines.

alternatives.name: Weblate
alternatives.desc: Serious Git-based localization with memory, glossaries, screenshots, suggestions and review; the interface means business.

facts.install: Hosted Weblate signup or the official Docker Compose deployment
facts.engines: Machine translation can connect to OpenAI/Azure OpenAI, DeepL, Google Cloud, Amazon Translate, Microsoft Translator, LibreTranslate, Baidu, Yandex, and other documented services.
facts.dataFormat: Translations, users, review state, memory, glossaries, and settings live in PostgreSQL; cloned source repositories and uploaded files live in persistent server volumes, with Valkey/Redis used for queues and caches.
facts.gapVsPaid: Weblate's Git-first core is strong but its vendor marketplace, enterprise workflow designer, integration catalog, polished hosted onboarding, and support are narrower than Crowdin's.
facts.setupBlocker: Cloud hosting is free only for qualifying libre projects; the general free route requires Docker, PostgreSQL, Valkey/Redis, domain/TLS, mail, repository credentials, backups, and upgrades.

alternatives.name: Mozilla Pontoon
alternatives.desc: A mature software-translation system with repository sync, suggestions and review, provided you are willing to operate it properly.

facts.install: Docker setup is documented for development; production deployment must be adapted from Mozilla/Heroku-style infrastructure
facts.dataFormat: Projects sync translations to version-control repositories, while users, suggestions, reviews, translation memory, and job state live in Pontoon's server databases and caches; Mozilla's public instance is not a general hosted service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Pontoon is built for Mozilla-style community localization and lacks Crowdin's general-purpose hosted onboarding, integration marketplace, vendor management, automation, and supported deployment.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is that the official Docker stack is explicitly not for production and the project does not provide a turnkey supported deployment for arbitrary operators.

alternatives.name: Accent
alternatives.desc: A lean collaborative string editor with history, rollback and CLI sync, minus Crowdin's integration department.

facts.install: Run the published Docker image with an external PostgreSQL database and production environment variables
facts.dataFormat: Projects, languages, strings, translations, comments, history, and users live in PostgreSQL; application configuration and secrets live on the server.
facts.gapVsPaid: Accent is a lean string database without Crowdin's broad file and repository integrations, translation memory depth, marketplace, workflow automation, and enterprise administration.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a production Elixir web deployment with Docker, external PostgreSQL, SECRET_KEY_BASE and authentication configuration, TLS, mail, backups, and upgrades; the old standalone Accent CLI is archived.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Team plan and a small-team string-management system DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Crowdin in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Drizzle ORM, and one optional machine-translation API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: manage a software localization project's translation keys with file sync, a glossary, and reviews, preserve context, import and export standard files, and publish approved strings.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Implement projects, locales, keys, namespaces, descriptions, screenshots, translations, and review status.
Import and export JSON, YAML, PO, and XLIFF while preserving placeholders and plural forms.
Add glossary checks, missing-string filters, translation memory, comments, and reviewer assignment.
Use machine translation only on selected strings and show provider, cost, and source text before approval.
Provide token-authenticated pull and push endpoints for CI with an immutable change log.
Add backups, locale deletion safeguards, and a pseudo-localization preview.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out a translator labor marketplace.
Deliberately leave out a global website translation proxy.
Deliberately leave out enterprise integrations, legal translation assurance, and round-the-clock support.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
